transcript.text: What is observability? Observability is
a way to find out what's happening
inside a complex system. Modern apps run
across many services, APIs, and
containers. So when something breaks,
you depend on three core signals:
metrics, logs, and traces. Metrics are
numbers that reflect system health like
CPU, latency, throughput, memory, etc.
Logs are detailed event messages that
tell you exactly what happened and why.
And lastly, traces show you the complete
path a request takes across multiple
services to know where the request
failed or slowed down. When you bring
metrics, logs, and traces together,
observability can help you answer
critical questions like where did the
request fail? Which microservices is
causing slowdown? Is the issue in code
infrastructure or any other dependency
and many other questions. So in short,
observability helps engineers debug
faster and understand system behavior
more clearly whenever there's an issue.
Subscribe.
